title: How Sam Bankman-Fried Actually Lost $8 Billion
hook: At 29, he was worth as much as $26 billion. A year later he had nothing, and $8 billion of customer money was simply gone -- inside an exchange he built himself, from an apartment.
body:
Sam Bankman-Fried graduated MIT with a physics degree in 2014, traded at Jane Street Capital, then left in 2017 to found the crypto trading firm Alameda Research out of a Berkeley apartment. In 2019 he co-founded the crypto exchange FTX with MIT classmate Gary Wang, with Caroline Ellison running Alameda and Nishad Singh running engineering. By January 2022 a funding round valued FTX at $32 billion, and Bankman-Fried's own fortune was estimated as high as $26 billion -- one of the youngest billionaires alive, fronted by a Super Bowl ad and endorsement deals with Tom Brady, Gisele Bundchen and Steph Curry. Behind it, Bankman-Fried had directed Gary Wang to build a secret exception into FTX's code letting Alameda -- nominally just another customer -- run an effectively unlimited negative balance, roughly a $65 billion line of credit, without the margin calls any other account faced. Roughly $10 billion in customer funds moved from FTX to Alameda, backed by FTX's own token, FTT. On November 2, 2022, CoinDesk published a leaked Alameda balance sheet showing its assets were mostly FTT. On November 6, Binance CEO Changpeng Zhao announced Binance would dump its FTT holdings, triggering a bank run: $6 billion in withdrawal requests in 72 hours, a trading halt on November 8, and Binance walking away from a rescue deal on November 9. FTX, Alameda and roughly 130 affiliated companies filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on November 11, 2022. Bankman-Fried was arrested in Nassau, the Bahamas, on December 12, 2022, and DOJ unsealed an eight-count indictment the next day. Gary Wang and Caroline Ellison pleaded guilty that December; Nishad Singh pleaded guilty soon after. At trial (Oct 3-Nov 2, 2023), Ellison testified Bankman-Fried directed her to use customer funds to cover losses, fund investments, buy real estate and make political donations. A jury convicted Bankman-Fried on all seven counts on November 2, 2023. On March 28, 2024, Judge Lewis Kaplan sentenced him to 25 years and ordered $11 billion in forfeiture; Ellison was sentenced to 2 years on September 24, 2024. This is what DOJ and SEC records, CoinDesk's reporting and the trial record say happened.
